subject: LATAM invoice split + SKU duplication for Marketplace private offer
messages:
From: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@acme-latam.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: DistribuCloud LLC <procurement@distribucloud.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Private offer for LATAM subsidiaries — invoicing and SKU mapping question

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Acme LATAM is excited about Redwood. We have a tricky procurement requirement from our finance and legal teams and wanted to check feasibility before we move to a private offer. Two items: 

1) Invoice splitting: Acme operates three legal entities (Mexico, Colombia, Chile). Our procurement team needs invoices issued locally to each entity for tax/regulatory reasons. We'd like Redwood (or through AWS Marketplace) to produce split invoices so each country is billed separately, even though the private offer would cover the consolidated commitment.

2) SKU duplication / local tax: For local tax reporting the marketplace SKU needs to be duplicated per country (same pricing, different SKU suffix) so our ERP can map spend by legal entity. Will that break the private-offer configuration or channel margin calculations for our reseller (DistribuCloud)?

I attached a draft SKU map and a short PDF that explains our billing flow. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a split-invoice flow and still provide a reseller margin to DistribuCloud (they're our channel partner for LATAM)? If not, we need to understand the recommended alternative to keep the reseller margin intact.

Appreciate a quick sanity check — our procurement deadline is end of month.

Regards,
Maria Ortiz
Head of Cloud Procurement — Acme LATAM
Mobile: +52 55 1234 5678

Attachments: acme_latam_sku_map.xlsx, proposed_invoice_split_v1.pdf
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@acme-latam.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, DistribuCloud LLC <procurement@distribucloud.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Oct 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer for LATAM subsidiaries — invoicing and SKU mapping question

Maria — thanks for the clear write-up and the attachments (received). Short answer: we can support a workable approach but it depends on two things — marketplace constraints (AWS/GCP) and how DistribuCloud needs margin to be reflected in invoicing.

High-level options we see: 
- Option A — Single private offer with splitter/billing routing: Redwood configures the private offer at the consolidated account level; invoicing is routed post-fact to local entities (requires distributor/partner to be set up for pass-through invoicing). This preserves a single commitment and lets us apply a channel margin to DistribuCloud as an operational rebate/credit.
- Option B — SKU aliasing per country + single private offer: create country-specific SKU aliases (MX/CO/CL suffixes) that map back to one meter under the hood. This satisfies ERP mapping but means reseller margin calculations need to be performed on the alias-to-master mapping — a small ops lift but doable.

We need Ben (channel ops) and Laura (rev ops) on the thread to confirm feasibility and to call out any constraints from AWS Marketplace (there are some limits on how many SKUs can be aliased and how billing flows are emitted). Ben — can you validate whether AWS private offers allow invoice-level split (Option A) for linked accounts, and whether aliasing SKUs will break reporting for a reseller margin path? Laura — if we go with Option B, what's the minimum mapping you need from Acme (e.g., expected monthly units per alias) to size the revenue waterfall?

If you can share expected monthly spend and a quick mapping of which BU/legal entity pays which percentage, that will get us to a proforma quickly. I'll also reach out to AWS Seller Support in parallel.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@acme-latam.com>, DistribuCloud LLC <procurement@distribucloud.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer for LATAM subsidiaries — invoicing and SKU mapping question

Vivek / Maria — quick operational note from channel ops: 

- AWS Marketplace: private offers are tied to a single seller (us) and a specific buyer account. Linked account invoicing can be done via consolidated billing / payer accounts. That supports issuing charges to linked accounts, but AWS still emits a single marketplace invoice from the seller side and the payer does the split internally.

- For your use-case (local legal invoicing), we can do two things: (1) set the private offer against a consolidated payer and have Acme handle downstream invoice splitting (preferred from a quick turnaround perspective), or (2) implement a post-processing invoice split where Redwood prepares country invoices and routes them to local entities — this requires additional legal and tax review and a revenue-recognition pass-through.

- SKU aliasing: we can create meter aliases (e.g., REDWOOD-TOKEN-MX, REDWOOD-TOKEN-CO, REDWOOD-TOKEN-CL) that all map to the same internal meter. From a metering perspective that works, and we can generate reporting that ties alias usage back to the master SKU for margin calculations. Caveat: some marketplace reporting exports do not preserve alias metadata downstream; we'd need to maintain our own mapping table for reconciliation.

- Channel margin mechanics: to preserve a clean reseller margin for DistribuCloud, we recommend structuring the margin as a separate reseller rebate administered by Redwood (or via distributor billing). Typical starting point for LATAM is 12–18% depending on contract length; we can model at 15% for the initial proforma.

Action items for Acme: share expected monthly units per alias and confirm DistribuCloud's seller/reseller ID (so we can map payouts).

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Channel Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@acme-latam.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer for LATAM subsidiaries — invoicing and SKU mapping question

Thanks — helpful. A few clarifications and attachments in response: 

- I've attached the SKU map (same file) with estimated monthly units per country and our current ERP codes. We expect ~$85k/month consolidated consumption year 1 (MX 50%, CO 30%, CL 20%).
- DistribuCloud's reseller ID: DC-98765 (they can confirm if you need a contact).
- Prefer Option A (private offer + post-transaction split) if we can get Redwood to generate the country invoices and include reseller margin line items for DistribuCloud. That simplifies our AP flow.

If Redwood can produce country-level invoices and manage the margin payout as a separate rebate, legal will move faster. If tax/legal says Redwood cannot re-issue invoices to local legal entities, we can fall back to consolidated payer routing + Acme internal split. Please let us know the likely timing for a proforma and any additional docs you need for legal/tax review.

Best,
Maria

Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Next steps and proforma timeline — Acme LATAM private offer

Maria / team — pulling threads together and proposing concrete next steps: 

1) Laura will build a proforma at 15% reseller margin (will show both Route A: Redwood-issued country invoices + margin rebate; and Route B: consolidated payer with Acme internal split + rebate to DistribuCloud). Expect initial proforma within 48 hours.

2) Ben will open an ops ticket with AWS Marketplace Seller Support to confirm whether Redwood can programmatically emit country-level invoices under our T&Cs (this is the gating legal/tax question). Ben — please include the DistribuCloud reseller ID and Acme payer account number in the ticket.

3) Maria — once you confirm the DistribuCloud contact, we'll add them to the payout onboarding flow. Also, please share any local tax certificates that the Redwood legal team should see for Mexico/Colombia/Chile (if you expect Redwood to re-issue invoices).

4) I'll schedule a 30-min call Friday to walk through the proforma and agree on the mechanism. Proposed time: Fri 10:00am Mexico City time. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks all — small note on timing: if we end up needing Redwood to re-issue local invoices we'll need ~3 weeks for legal/tax review; if we use the consolidated-payer fallback we can move in days. We'll aim for the quicker path but keep the local-invoice ask as an escalatable option.

Vivek
